title: [AUG-111] Windows direct system audio capture via ffmpeg dshow loopback device
why_we_need_this:
Follow-up to AUG-105. Direct (picker-free) system audio capture currently exists only on macOS; on Windows the capability probe in @server/src/services/systemCapture.ts always returns method 'none', so Settings greys out "System (direct)" and every recording goes through the getDisplayMedia screen picker. Windows users have the same friction the macOS work removed.

ffmpeg has no native WASAPI loopback input, but Windows commonly exposes a loopback as an ordinary DirectShow capture device: the driver-provided "Stereo Mix" input (Realtek and most onboard audio; must be enabled in Sound settings > Recording) or a virtual cable such as VB-Cable ("CABLE Output"). These behave exactly like BlackHole does on macOS, so the AUG-105 structure (probe → start/stop lifecycle → self-test → offset alignment → session upload by captureId) can be reused unchanged.

Design:
1. Add CaptureMethod 'dshow-loopback'. On win32 the probe runs `ffmpeg -hide_banner -list_devices true -f dshow -i dummy`, parses the audio device names from stderr, and picks the first matching /stereo mix|what u hear|cable output|voicemeeter|virtual.*cable|loopback/i. Store the exact device name (not an index) for the -i argument.
2. startCapture for 'dshow-loopback': `ffmpeg -f dshow -i audio="<name>" -ac 1 -ar 16000 -c:a pcm_s16le -y <captureId>.wav`, stopped with the same graceful sequence as the BlackHole path (SIGINT-first per AUG-110; on Windows Node's kill('SIGINT') is a hard terminate, so send 'q' on stdin first and only then kill).
3. Run the existing self-test (AUG-106) on win32 too, so a Stereo Mix that is present but disabled or muted shows "silent" with a hint to enable it.
4. Hints: no device found → "Enable 'Stereo Mix' in Sound settings > Recording (right-click > Show Disabled Devices), or install VB-Cable and set 'CABLE Input' as the default output device."
5. Client needs no logic change: resolveSystemAudioSource already unlocks 'system' when systemCapture is true. Update the Windows-only wording in the Settings status text and notices where it says capture is macOS-only.
6. Docs: architecture and preferences READMEs drop the "macOS-only" statements and document the dshow probe, device-name matching and the stdin 'q' stop rule on Windows.
acceptance_criteria:
- On Windows with Stereo Mix (or a VB-Cable "CABLE Output") enabled, GET /api/capture/capabilities returns systemCapture true, method 'dshow-loopback', the matched device name in the hint, and a selfTest result.
- With System audio source = System (or Auto) on that machine, pressing Record produces a dual-track [Me]/[Them] session with no screen picker or share confirmation.
- On Windows with no loopback device, the probe returns method 'none' with the enable-Stereo-Mix / VB-Cable hint and recording still uses the browser picker (no regression).
- POST /api/capture/stop on Windows returns a WAV with a valid header (ffprobe duration within 100 ms of the capture length).
- Unit tests cover the dshow device-list parser and the loopback-name matcher with a realistic stderr fixture (Stereo Mix, microphone, and CABLE Output entries).
- macOS behaviour and tests from AUG-105..110 are unchanged.
- Settings status line and client notices no longer say direct capture is macOS-only.
- project-context/architecture and project-context/preferences READMEs document the Windows dshow path.
important_constraints:
- No new native dependencies; ffmpeg is already mandatory.
- Keep the loopbackOnly guard on all capture endpoints.
- Do not attempt WASAPI loopback in this task; a helper binary is a separate follow-up if dshow proves insufficient.
